patterns_detected.description: Single-item reads by the full primary key: GetItem, or BatchGetItem for up to 100 keys and 16 MB, at single-digit-millisecond latency at any scale (Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, Working with items; Amazon DynamoDB API Reference, BatchGetItem).

Queries that pin a partition key value and bound a sort key by a range: a DynamoDB Query with a KeyConditionExpression, returned in sort-key order, at most 1 MB per page; with a local secondary index an item collection is limited to 10 GB (Amazon DynamoDB API Reference, Query; Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, Local secondary indexes).

Frequent writes that address their items by key (INSERT, or UPDATE/DELETE by key): PutItem, UpdateItem and DeleteItem write one item by its primary key, and capacity scales with the table's partitions (Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, Working with items).

Time-ordered data with timestamp-based range reads. Maps to DynamoDB with entity ID as partition key and timestamp as sort key. TTL for automatic expiry (Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, Time to Live).

Small, rarely written reference tables read by key (feature flags, config, lookup tables): GetItem or BatchGetItem on the key, with DynamoDB Accelerator for microsecond reads at an extra node cost (Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, Working with items; In-memory acceleration with DAX).

Parent-child relationship where the cardinality can be reasoned about at design time. A partition key value's item collection has no size limit unless the table has a local secondary index (then 10 GB). The bound is domain-driven (e.g., order → items, user → addresses) (Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, Local secondary indexes). Large item collections may need creative sort key design for efficient range queries.

Tables frequently accessed together in the same queries (co-access frequency > 50 calls/hour). Strong signal for denormalization into one item collection that a single Query returns (Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, Best practices for modeling relational data).

anti_patterns_detected.description: A read more frequent than once a minute that pins no column to a value, so no partition key value can address it whatever the key design. On DynamoDB that is a Scan, which reads every item and consumes read capacity for every item it reads, not only the ones it returns (Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, Scanning tables).
anti_patterns_detected.recommendation: The schema design agent will replace these scans with targeted Query or GetItem operations. Verify the generated access patterns cover all flagged queries. Remaining scans may need a GSI or access pattern redesign.

anti_patterns_detected.description: GROUP BY, HAVING, or an aggregate over rows no key anchors or over a join (one key's COUNT or SUM is a Query on that key, not this pattern). DynamoDB has no server-side aggregation: a Query or Scan can only count the items it reads (Select = COUNT), so a grouped result needs the application layer, pre-computed aggregates or a separate analytics store (Amazon DynamoDB API Reference, Query).
anti_patterns_detected.recommendation: Pre-compute aggregates on write (DynamoDB Streams + Lambda), or export to S3/Athena for analytics.

footnotes: DynamoDB reads are priced eventually consistent, except transactions, which are priced at transactional rates.

pricing_assumptions: On-demand capacity mode (no provisioned throughput), on average load
Reads billed on the bytes each call returns (rows times the table's average row size), rounded up to 4 KB
Writes billed on each item's size (the table's average row), rounded up to 1 KB; an update's new size is not collected, so the larger of the item before and after it is taken as that average
71 reads priced eventually consistent (0.5 RRU per 4 KB)
22 writes priced at the standard rate (1 WRU per 1 KB per item)
1 multi-item write (2 to 100 items, kept atomic as one TransactWriteItems call) priced transactional (2 WRU per 1 KB per item)
Global secondary indexes are not modelled: their write and storage costs are not included
No DAX, backups, or global tables included
